title: Introduce fast-presubmit lane, dep-throttle orchestrator, and lint-adapter
author: Marina Lopez
release_notes:
- Add a fast-presubmit GitHub Actions lane for low-latency feedback on small diffs.
- Deploy `dep-throttle` service to limit external dependency upgrade churn during high-traffic windows.
- Introduce `lint-adapter` to translate repo lint rules into a faster, staged runner so linting can be split between quick and full checks.
description:
Title: Introduce fast-presubmit lane, dep-throttle orchestrator, and lint-adapter

Summary: This PR adds a low-latency presubmit lane designed to give developers fast feedback for small, focused changes while offloading heavyweight checks to staged lanes. It also introduces a lightweight 'dep-throttle' orchestrator that gates automated dependency rollouts to avoid mass churn during peak CI usage, and a lint-adapter shim that lets us run a slim quick-lint for premerge and a full-lint in the nightly pipeline. The goals are faster inner-loop developer feedback, fewer CI collisions during dependency upgrades, and clearer separation between quick checks and full verification runs.

Motivation and context: Over the last quarter we observed increased median feedback time for small PRs due to a growing integration test matrix and aggressive automatic dependency rollouts. ENG-1287 captured the developer frustration with slow presubmit feedback. ENG-1303 proposed isolating dependency upgrade traffic and staged lint execution so that small edits (docs, comments, small refactors) get sub-5m feedback. This work implements the orchestration and the GitHub Actions lane changes to realize that.

What changed (high-level):
- Add `.github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml` — a slim presubmit action that runs: staged-quick-lint, unit tests (fast shards), small integration smoke (file-change aware), and a lightweight cache warm.
- Add `tools/dep-throttle/` — small Go service and a cli used by the dependency automation pipeline to detect ongoing rollout windows and delay non-urgent upgrades.
- Add `scripts/lint-adapter.ts` — Node shim that maps existing eslint/rulesets into fast/run-on-delta mode and reports in the same annotation format as full-lint.
- Update `internal/ci/runner.go` to introduce 'lane' concept (fast, full, nightly) and expose lane hints to the executor.
- Docs: `docs/presubmit.md` describing the lanes and contributor guidance.
- Tests: Add `tests/ci/presubmit_fastpath_test.go` and integration smoke harness additions to cover the new lane behavior.

Commits (summary):
- 8a2c9f2  Add presubmit-fastpath workflow and quick-lint runner hooks.
- b4f1d17  Implement dep-throttle service and CLI gate.
- c1e3a88  Add lint-adapter shim and integrate with annotations.
- d9f7b21  Expose lane hints in internal/ci runner and add unit tests.
- f7a2b05  Docs and contributor guidance; add e2e smoke to nightly pipeline.

Files changed (high-level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit-fastpath.yml
- tools/dep-throttle/main.go, tools/dep-throttle/README.md, tools/dep-throttle/config.yaml.example
- scripts/lint-adapter.ts
- internal/ci/runner.go, internal/ci/runner_test.go
- docs/presubmit.md
- tests/ci/presubmit_fastpath_test.go, tests/ci/smoke/fastpath_sample.yaml

Key implementation notes:
- presubmit-fastpath uses path-aware triggers: only runs on PRs where changed files match a predefined fast-path globs file (docs/, examples/, small package changes). Changes to core service code continue to trigger full lanes.
- dep-throttle exposes a simple HTTP API for the dependency-automation bot to query current window state; it implements a token-bucket style limiter so multiple concurrent upgrades are serialized and retried with backoff. The default config keeps throttle off-peak and moderately aggressive during business hours.
- lint-adapter performs delta-based linting: it runs eslint only on changed files and returns annotations in the same format as full-lint so the Console and PR show consistent feedback. It intentionally avoids expensive autofix passes in the quick lane.

Review flow and decisions:
- Request: Please review the runner API additions and the dep-throttle semantics (Ruben Park).
- Main debate: whether to centralize presubmit triggers in a single repository-level glob file vs. per-repo YAML. We elected for a single source-of-truth under `docs/presubmit.md` with a nightly job that validates the globs.
- Security: dep-throttle is read-only by default and requires the automation bot token for write operations; Aisha audited the service and recommended a short-lived token pattern to limit blast radius.

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Ruben Park (reviewer): "Runner changes look ok, but can we avoid adding a new long-lived goroutine per PR? Concerned about memory under high parallelism."
- Marina Lopez (author): "Good catch — updated runner.go to use a pooled worker per executor rather than per PR; tests updated (runner_test.go) to simulate 200 concurrent jobs."
- Aisha Patel (reviewer): "dep-throttle config is reasonable; please add an opt-out label for repo owners who want immediate rollouts."
- Marina Lopez: "Added `dep-upgrade/skip-throttle` label support and documented behavior in README for dep-throttle."
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "lint-adapter annotations look fine; add a smoke harness so we can validate the annotation format in the Console parser."
- Marina Lopez: "Added tests/ci/smoke/fastpath_sample.yaml and console-parser wrapper in scripts/ to validate annotation format."

CI:
- Initial run: unit (pass, 8m), fast-integration (fail, flake in smoke harness), lint (pass quick-lint), build (pass), e2e (skipped for fastpath).
- Fix: Addressed race in smoke harness (test flakiness) and re-ran CI. Final: all checks pass.

Merging and rollout:
- Merge method: squash and merge.
- Merged on 2026-03-04 by Marina Lopez after reviewers approved and CI passed.
- Post-merge: presubmit-fastpath workflow was enabled in a staged rollout — initially opt-in for active contributors via a repo label; after monitoring 48 hours with no regressions we flipped default to on for non-core directories.

Operational notes and follow-ups:
- Follow-up ticket (ENG-1340): add telemetry to dep-throttle to capture delay/queue metrics and expose them in Console.
- Follow-up ticket (ENG-1341): add an admin UI for temporary throttle overrides behind SSO+audit logging.
- Follow-up ticket (ENG-1342): migrate monolith lint rules to staged rule-sets so the quick-lint remains stable at scale.

Why this is different from prior PRs: Instead of only trimming matrices or changing cache keys, this PR introduces an orchestrator artifact (dep-throttle) plus a runtime lane concept and a lint translation shim. The intent is to operationalize CI load management and give predictable developer feedback without sacrificing full verification for risky changes.

Notes for release and cross-team communication:
- Notify developer experience channel on Slack about the new fast lane and the label opt-in flow.
- Post guide in the contributor docs and update the onboarding checklist so new contributors understand why their PR may only run the fast lane.
- Dependency automation team to update their bot to check dep-throttle before opening batch upgrades.

Contact: Marina Lopez (author) for follow-up and troubleshooting.
